text:
nora: alert — sudden spike in model backend load and 5xx starting ~14:07 UTC. dashboards show prefix_cache.hit_rate collapsed from ~70% -> 9% in ~4m.
sam: rolling deploy to runtime-canary-7 finished at 14:05 (deploy #6201). suspect canary. infra-bot: deploy #6201 finished by @ci-bot at 2026-04-12T14:05:12Z — target=runtime-canary-7 image=redwood/runtime:canary-20260412-6201
kai: I shipped a small perf tweak to improve packing locality — it annotates requests with a transient field `affinity_tag` so the scheduler packs similar work together. That field should be metadata-only, not persisted.
mira: dump from kv service:
```
nkv.prefix_cache.hit_rate: 0.09
nkv.req_rate: 98k/min
nkv.write_ratio: 0.41
backend.inflight: 770
model.5xx: 3.9%
avg_latency_ms: 138
```
nora: if affinity_tag leaked into key serialization, every worker would generate different keys for same prefix -> fragmentation and near-zero hit rate. can we check keygen logs?
ops-bot: traced example keys:
```
# same prefix, model, only affinity differs
POST /kv/key {"prefix":"Summarize: ...","model":"rwd-13b","affinity_tag":"rack-A"} -> key: sha1:aa11...
POST /kv/key {"prefix":"Summarize: ...","model":"rwd-13b","affinity_tag":"rack-B"} -> key: sha1:bb22...
```
sam: that matches. affinity_tag slipped into the deterministic serialization path. this explains fragmentation across runtime instances.
kai: argh — I added affinity to the request proto then updated the serializer but missed the kv_key builder who imports the full request object. intended to be runtime-only, not part of key.
mira: mitigation plan: 1) pause prefix cache writes globally 2) disable reads on runtime-canary-7 3) scale up backend by +25% 4) revert canary patch or sanitize keygen so it ignores affinity_tag.
infra-bot: PATCH /api/feature-flags set prefix_cache_writes=false target=all by sam — applied
infra-bot: POST /api/feature-flags set prefix_cache_reads=false target=runtime-canary-7 by sam — applied
ops-bot: scaling action: model-backend-pool scaled +25% — applied
nora: metrics after toggles: hit_rate for stable pools steady ~71%; canary still low until reads off. backend inflight dropping from 770 -> 210 over 6m. avg latency back near baseline.
kai: prepping quick PR to remove affinity from key serialization and add explicit `key_schema_version` header so accidental additions fail fast.
mira: add canary test: on canary deploy, run key-diff harness that samples 5k recent prefixes and verifies keys stable vs baseline; fail deploy if mismatch > 0.2%. also add unit test that asserts serializer excludes transient fields (affinity_tag).
sam: incident INC-2026-0899 created. root cause: transient affinity_tag leaked into keygen -> cache fragmentation -> backend overload. contributing: lack of key-schema versioning and missing canary key-stability check.
ops-bot: Incident INC-2026-0899 status=stabilized assignees=[kai,nora,sam] next_meeting=2026-04-13T16:00:00Z
kai: will push revert + key-schema change in next 10m. also adding linter rule that flags request fields annotated `transient=true` being read by key builder.
nora: follow-ups: add alert on prefix_cache.hit_rate drop >25% absolute within 5m, document key-stability checklist, require cross-team review for any change touching request proto or serializer.
sam: good response — toggles + scale bought time. keep monitoring for 1h then close. great cross-team triage :thumbsup:
